title: Which Edge Closes the Cycle?

concept.title: Add the edges in the given order; the first edge whose ends are already connected is the one
body: A tree with `n` nodes has `n - 1` edges. Here one **extra** edge was added, so the graph has exactly one cycle, and removing **any** edge of that cycle would give a tree again. The task: print the extra edge, meaning the one among the cycle edges that appears **last** in the input.

Use union-find and add the edges **in the order of the input**. While the edges seen so far form a forest, each new edge joins two different groups (a *union*). At some moment an edge has both ends in the **same** group: it closes the cycle. Since the first `n - 1` or fewer edges before that moment were still a forest, all the other cycle edges came before this one, so it is the last cycle edge in the input, exactly the one asked for.

body.code:
for u, v in edges:
    if not union(u, v):             # the ends were already connected
        print(u, v)
        break

body: There is only one cycle in the whole graph, so there is exactly one such moment. Union by size and path compression make every operation almost constant, so the time is O(n * alpha(n)).

statement: The `n` edges join `n` nodes into a tree plus one extra edge, so the graph has exactly one cycle. Removing any edge of the cycle leaves a tree. Print the edge of the cycle that appears last in the input, written exactly as it appears in the input.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`: the number of nodes and also the number of edges.
Each of the next `n` lines has two numbers `u` and `v`: an edge between the nodes `u` and `v`.
outputFormat: Print the two numbers of the edge.
constraints: The edges are a tree on the nodes 1 to n with one extra edge added (so there is exactly one cycle).
There are no self-loops and no repeated edges.

examples.note: The three edges form a triangle; the last one is 2 3.
The cycle 1-2-3-4 is closed by the last edge: 1 4.

hints: Use union-find; start with every node as its own group.
Take the edges in the input order and merge the groups of the two ends.
The first edge whose ends are already in the same group is the answer.

explanation: With union-find the edges are added in input order; the first edge whose two ends are already in the same group closes the only cycle, and it is the last cycle edge in the input.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

parent = []
size = []

def find(x):
    while parent[x] != x:
        parent[x] = parent[parent[x]]
        x = parent[x]
    return x

def union(a, b):
    a, b = find(a), find(b)
    if a == b:
        return False
    if size[a] < size[b]:
        a, b = b, a
    parent[b] = a
    size[a] += size[b]
    return True

n = int(input())
edges = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]

parent.extend(range(n + 1))
size.extend([1] * (n + 1))
for u, v in edges:
    if not union(u, v):
        print(u, v)
        break
